Includes.description: Specify the fields that should be returned for the given entities. Object key needs to be the entity name, and the list of fields needs to be the value. Fields will not be included, if they are also specified in the excludes. Note that the include fields will only be stripped on the API-Level, consider using the `fields` parameter for performance reasons. To return a DAL extension, list the extension by its name (for example `myExtension`); the `extensions` wrapper is then kept automatically. Listing the keyword `extensions` returns all extensions.

info.description:
This endpoint reference contains an overview of all endpoints comprising the Shopware Admin API.

For a better overview, all CRUD-endpoints are hidden by default. If you want to show also CRUD-endpoints
add the query parameter `type=jsonapi`.
info.title: Shopware Admin API

post.description: Moves an order to another state with a `transition`, as the Administration does: from open, `process` (in progress) or `cancel`; from in progress, `complete`. Shopware mails the customer as its flows say, unless `sendMail` is false. Answers the order's new state, whose `technicalName` is `in_progress`, `completed`, `cancelled`, … A transition the order's state does not allow is refused, naming the ones it does.

parameters.description:
The `action_name` of the `state_machine_transition`. For example `process` if the order state should change from open to in progress.

Note: If you choose a transition that is not available, you will get an error that lists possible transitions for the current state.
parameters.name: transition

documentIds.description: A list of document identifiers that should be attached

internalComment.description: An optional internal comment that will be saved with the state transition.

mediaIds.description: A list of media identifiers that should be attached

sendMail.description: Controls if a mail should be sent to the customer.

stateFieldName.description: This is the state column within the order database table. There should be no need to change it from the default.

post.summary: Transition an order to a new state

post.description: Moves a delivery of an order (its ID among the order's `deliveries`) to another state with a `transition`, such as `ship` (shipped) or `cancel`. Answers the delivery's new state (`technicalName`). A transition the delivery's state does not allow is refused, naming the ones it does.

parameters.description:
The `action_name` of the `state_machine_transition`. For example `process` if the order state should change from open to in progress.

Note: If you choose a transition which is not possible, you will get an error that lists possible transition for the actual state.
parameters.name: transition

documentIds.description: A list of document identifiers that should be attached

internalComment.description: An optional internal comment that will be saved with the state transition.

mediaIds.description: A list of media identifiers that should be attached

sendMail.description: Controls if a mail should be send to the customer.

stateFieldName.description: This is the state column within the order delivery database table. There should be no need to change it from the default.

post.description: Moves a payment of an order (its ID among the order's `transactions`) to another state with a `transition`, such as `paid`, `refund` or `cancel`. It records the payment's state; it moves no money. Answers the payment's new state (`technicalName`). A transition the payment's state does not allow is refused, naming the ones it does.

post.description: Creates a customer: their `customerNumber`, `firstName`, `lastName` and `email`, the `groupId` and `salesChannelId` they belong to, and their `defaultBillingAddress` and `defaultShippingAddress` (each with `firstName`, `lastName`, `street`, `zipcode`, `city` and `countryId`). Search Entities finds the `customer-group`, `sales-channel` and `country` records.

get.description: Reads a customer by their ID.
get.summary: Detailed information about a Customer resource.

patch.description: Updates a customer with the fields given.

requestBody.description: Partially update information about a Customer resource.

patch.summary: Partially update information about a Customer resource.

patch.description: Updates a delivery of an order (its ID among the order's `deliveries`) with the fields given, such as its `trackingCodes`, a list that replaces the delivery's.

requestBody.description: Partially update information about a Order Delivery resource.

patch.summary: Partially update information about a Order Delivery resource.

get.description: Reads an order by its ID: its number, amounts, dates and the IDs of what it refers to. Its line items, deliveries and payments come back only from Search Orders with the order's ID in `ids` and `associations`.
get.summary: Detailed information about a Order resource.

patch.description: Updates an order with the fields given, such as its `customerComment`, `affiliateCode` or `customFields`. Its state is changed by Transition Order State.

requestBody.description: Partially update information about a Order resource.

patch.summary: Partially update information about a Order resource.

post.description: Creates a product: its `productNumber`, `stock`, `name`, `taxId` and `price` (per currency, its `currencyId`, `gross`, `net` and `linked`; Search Entities finds the `tax` and `currency` records). A variant gives its product's ID as `parentId`, and inherits what it leaves out. An `id` of your own (32 hex digits) lets a workflow look the product up when a create's outcome is unknown.

delete.description: Deletes a product or a variant for good.

get.description: Reads a product or a variant by its ID. A variant leaves empty what it inherits from its parent product.
get.summary: Detailed information about a Product resource.

patch.description: Updates a product or a variant with the fields given: `stock`, `price`, `active`, `name` or any other.

requestBody.description: Partially update information about a Product resource.

patch.summary: Partially update information about a Product resource.

post.description: Searches customers with Shopware's search criteria: `filter` (as `[{"type": "equals", "field": "email", "value": "jane@example.com"}]`), `sort`, `limit` and `page` (from 1), or `ids`. Their addresses come back only when `associations` asks for them (`{"addresses": {}}`).

Searches orders with Shopware's search criteria: `filter` (as `[{"type": "equals", "field": "orderNumber", "value": "10001"}]`, or a `range` of `orderDateTime`), `sort`, `limit` and `page` (from 1), or `ids`. What an order refers to comes back only when `associations` asks for it: `{"lineItems": {}, "deliveries": {}, "transactions": {}}` for its line items, its deliveries (with their tracking codes and state) and its payments.

Searches products with Shopware's search criteria: `filter` (as `[{"type": "equals", "field": "productNumber", "value": "SW10001"}]`), `sort`, `limit` and `page` (from 1), or `ids`. A variant's `parentId` is its product's; it inherits what it leaves empty. What a product refers to comes back only when `associations` asks for it (`{"categories": {}, "media": {}}`).
